Retrieval question 1: Using only the supplied records, explain which service should handle a delayed job and whether replay is safe. Cite record IDs and separate facts from assumptions.
[POL-0-A, revised 2026-09-12] The Cedar ingestion service accepts at-least-once deliveries and records the pair (tenant_id, event_id) in the same transaction as the business update. Duplicate pairs return the previously committed result. Event IDs are unique only within a tenant. The API timeout is 15 seconds; a timeout does not establish whether a transaction committed.
[RUN-0-B, revised 2026-10-01] The Birch dispatcher retries HTTP 429 and 503 responses with exponential backoff and jitter, capped at 60 seconds. The Retry-After header takes precedence when it is valid. After five attempts the event moves to the dead-letter queue with its original identifiers and last error. The dispatcher must preserve tenant-local order.
[INC-0-C, incident 2026-10-08] At 09:42 an operator replayed a failed batch with newly generated event IDs. Twelve updates were applied twice. Recovery restored the old IDs, reconciled affected rows, and disabled the replay command's regenerate-identifiers option. No data was lost. The observed delay was caused by a downstream 503 response, not by queue capacity.
[OLD-0-D, archived 2025-06-03] An obsolete deployment guide recommends retrying every timeout immediately and generating a new event ID for each request. The guide is explicitly superseded by POL-0-A and RUN-0-B.
Explain the timeline, conflicting advice, operational owner, safe replay command parameters, and checks needed before declaring recovery. If the records do not specify a command name or an individual owner's name, say so rather than inventing one.
